definitions.explanation: A way of cooking rice in plenty of boiling water, like pasta, then draining off the excess water and steaming it briefly. It is the usual method in parts of South and Southeast Asia, and in Japan it is mentioned in cooking and history contexts, in contrast to the standard absorption method ({炊|た}き{干|ぼ}し).

examples.japanese: {湯取|ゆと}り{法|ほう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦ご{飯|はん}→ご飯：00776_gohan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{炊|た}く→炊く：02127_taku⟧。
examples.english: I cook rice by the boil-and-drain method.

examples.english: In India, the boil-and-drain method is common.

examples.japanese: {湯取|ゆと}り{法|ほう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{炊|た}く→炊く：02127_taku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{余分|よぶん}→余分：03667_yobun⟧な⟦でんぷん→デンプン：11028_denpun⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{流|なが}れ{出|で}て、さらっとした⟦ご{飯|はん}→ご飯：00776_gohan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Cooking rice by boiling and draining washes away the excess starch, so the rice comes out light and separate.

notes:
⟦{湯|ゆ}→湯：01740_yu⟧ (hot water) + ⟦{取|と}り→取る：00565_toru⟧ (taking off) + ⟦{法|ほう}→法：13620_hou⟧ (method). Not related to ⟦ゆとり→ゆとり：10652_yutori⟧ (room, leeway), though it is pronounced the same.

- ⟦{炊|た}き→炊く：02127_taku⟧{干|ぼ}し: the absorption method, Japan's standard way of cooking rice
